brief: Early-20th-century one- and two-storey brick grocery block on a streetcar avenue: a wide plate-glass front with a transom band, a flat parapet with a painted name strip, and a plain side wall facing a gravel lot; worn, part of a struggling neighbourhood strip.

facade.notes: Salem Avenue, Dayton (1915-30s): a neighbourhood commercial strip on a trolley-bus line (the overhead wires) -- one- and two-storey brick shops, several boarded, a 'STYLE SHOP', a terra-cotta-faced block; a wide street

why.note: a streetcar-line commercial strip: shops at every stop
Dayton's west-side streetcar strips emptied after the 1960s
